speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of a high fever, seizure, and now a generalized nonpruritic rash. To help me understand what is happening, can you tell me exactly when the fever and seizure started and how long they lasted?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola).

The clinical presentation of a high fever, seizure, and a generalized nonpruritic rash spreading from the trunk to the extremities is highly suggestive of measles. Although the patient's immunizations are up to date, vaccine failure can occur. To confirm this diagnosis, I am requesting a Measles Serology test.
